description: RF-601..RF-604, RF-621: the planner's two answers for the hand-off package of the planning integration test. First the plan: requirements that cite supported cards, one that cites a card with no supported claim and an unknown id, one holding hostile Markdown and HTML, an entity mapping without a supported card, and a task in a phase that does not exist. The two tasks that are kept state an invariant, a risk class, the guards they add and review probes (RF-630, RF-635). Second the product requirements document: features that cite FEAT cards (one a card with no supported claim, one holding hostile Markdown and HTML), rules that cite BR cards (one citing a FEAT card), an out-of-scope item, and a role and a non-functional item holding hostile Markdown and HTML. Written by hand for the fake provider; no real provider was called. The third call is the data model (RF-623, P3-17): tables that map supported ENT claims, a column whose legacy claim is not supported, a type that is not a type name, a name that is not an identifier, a foreign key to a missing table and a dropped field. The fourth call is the target flows (RF-625, P3-19): FLOW-001 mapped with a step to a component the architecture lacks, a rejected step, a step of another card and a repeated step; FLOW-002 out of scope with a reason; FLOW-077, which no card has; FLOW-003 left unmentioned. Used only by runs whose cards include FLOW cards. The fifth call is the API contract (RF-624, P3-18), made only when the brief names a front end and a FEAT or FLOW card is verified: operations that serve FEAT and FLOW cards (one also naming an ENT card and an unknown card, one marked public although it carries customers), a name that is not an identifier, a path that climbs, an operation that serves a card nobody verified and a summary holding hostile Markdown and HTML.
